elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once in any twelve-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly limits inspection to “no more than once in any twelve (12) month period.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least thirty days’ prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice.”

elements.element: Audits must occur during Customer’s business hours.
elements.evidence: Inspection is limited to “the Company’s normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection right is granted directly to HDI’s General Manager, with no requirement that the inspecting party be independent.

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The operative clause contains no confidentiality requirement applicable to the inspecting party.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause requires HDI to bear all fees it incurs in connection with the inspection, without any cost-shifting to Customer; this is more protective of Customer than the permitted 5% exception.

elements.element: The audit right must not include direct access to Customer systems.
elements.evidence: The clause permits inspection of relevant records but does not expressly prohibit direct access to Customer systems or specify a records-production-only process.

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The rolling twelve-month limitation is at least as restrictive as a once-per-year limitation.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least fifteen days’ notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires thirty days’ prior written notice, exceeding the fifteen-day fallback.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause requires HDI to bear all fees it incurs in connection with the inspection, without cost-shifting even if an underpayment exceeds 10%; this is more protective of Customer.

result.reason: The redline adds only the frequency limitation needed to complete the fallback position; the existing thirty-day written notice, business-hours restriction, and HDI-paid fees remain effective. It does not satisfy the preferred position because the operative text authorizes HDI’s General Manager—not an independent, confidentiality-bound auditor—and does not prohibit direct system access. The amendment preserves the limited records-inspection right and introduces no unrelated commercial term or contradiction.
